title: Input gain trim + pad control on standalone audio settings
acceptanceCriteria: Input gain slider (continuous, -24 dB to +12 dB, default 0 dB) in the audio settings UI
-20 dB Pad toggle button next to the slider for quick attenuation of hot sources (laptop mic arrays, line-level signals)
Gain is applied in the standalone audio capture path BEFORE samples reach fx_engine_process (pre-engine, not a new engine API)
Plugin build path is unaffected — hosts provide their own channel gain, the plugin does not need this
Input meter in GUI reflects the post-gain signal so users see the effect of the slider
Setting persists between runs — saved to the user-config / last-session file so relaunching keeps the level
Real-time safe: multiplication is a simple scalar in the capture callback, no mallocs, no locks
notes: Discovered 2026-04-18 during TASK-365 verification. Laptop mic arrays on Fedora 44 / PipeWire run at high system gain intended for far-field voice; plugging that into an amp-sim chain clips the input meter instantly. Real interfaces (iRig/Scarlett) won't have this issue but the app still needs a simple input trim so users can run off the laptop mic without re-digging pactl volumes. Keep it standalone-only — the plugin doesn't need pre-gain since the DAW supplies that.
